title: WPMS/1938/2018 of Amit Saini Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT
NAINITAL
Writ Petition (M/S) No. 1938 Of 2017

Amit Saini Ö Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand & Others Ö Respondents
Ms. Sonia Chawla, Advocate, for the petitioner.
Mr. Yogesh Pandey, Additional CSC, for the
State/respondents no. 1 to 5.

Petitioner before this Court is a person who
was allotted a liquor shop at Roorkee. Thereafter the
petitioner made some defaults in payment of ìexcise
dutyî to the Excise Department and, consequently,
now the amount of the excise duty is being recovered
as the arrears of land revenue and in that process
the property of the petitioner is being auctioned.

2. The case of the petitioner is that though
the shop was allotted in his name but it was being
run by respondents no. 6 and 7. It was being done by
the partnership firm named M/s Aahana Liquors
Partnership Firm in which petitioner was inducted
subsequently as 1 per cent partner.
3. That may be so, but the fact of the matter
is that no interference is liable to be made in the
present matter as far as the recovery of excise duty is
concerned as such prayer cannot be granted in a writ

2
petition as the liquor shop was admittedly allotted to
the petitioner and the petitioner ought not to have
transferred or let out the shop to a third person as
this is the violation of the conditions of allotment.
Therefore, on the face of it, the petitioner has violated
the conditions of the allotment of the liquor shop. In
case, the liquor shop was being run by a partnership
firm, the petitioner was admittedly a partner in that
firm.
4. Hence, no interference is called for in the
present matter. Writ petition is hereby dismissed in
limine.

5. Having made the determination, however,
the Secretary, Excise, Government of Uttarakhand is
hereby directed to conduct an independent enquiry
into the alleged deeds of respondents no. 6 and 7
which are the so called partners of the firm and in
case the allegations made by the petitioner are found
to be correct, let an appropriate action be taken in
accordance with law.
 (Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
 11.7.2018
